review_reference: Owner decision Q43 of 2026-11-11 (OCR learning: rules switch on only after 5 identical corrections from 3 staff, suggestions only, sensitive classes excluded, kill switch per rule set) and the coordinator's answers of the same day; to be signed by the owner (0118 and 0119 separately).
evidence: Migration 0118 and 0119. 0118_ocr_correction_observations.sql plus its runtime-grants.sql block. WHAT IT DOES: two new tables in schema ocr, granted to no runtime role (row-level security forced, one owner policy each): ocr.learning_key (one row, a 32-byte key made by the migration with gen_random_bytes; no deployment secret, coordinator decision of 2026-11-11) and ocr.correction_observations (facility, field class, SHA-256 digest of the value the AI reading gave, the closed-list value the reviewer saved or NULL, HMAC-SHA-256 of the staff account under that key, HMAC of the validation id, time; the digest itself is stored as its HMAC under the key, so no row can be checked against guessed text or joined to a validation without the key). Nothing read from a paper is stored: ocr-api sends a digest, never the text, and only drug-list, strength, frequency-code, lab-test and lab-unit values. Two SECURITY DEFINER functions: ocr.record_correction_observations (OCR API; a staff session holding ocr.validation.write, its own accepted validation of the last 10 minutes, at most 200 well-formed entries, none a sensitive value by ocr.learning_value_sensitive, the database's copy of ocr-api's sensitive list hid.ocr.sensitive/v2 (an immutable SQL function granted to no role, kept identical by a spec); idempotent per validation and key; also deletes rows older than 180 days) and ocr.purge_correction_observations (OCR worker account only; 180-day retention, oldest first). KEY NOTE: database dumps and backups carry the HMAC key with the rows; the key only pseudonymises staff counts (it never identifies anyone by itself and protects no patient data), so this is accepted. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: nothing existing changes; today's ocr-api, ocr-worker and identity-api images never call the new functions. LOCKS: only the new tables and SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.facilities (the foreign key); no existing row read or written. TESTS: services/ehr-api/test/database/ocr-correction-observations.integration.sql (48 cases as the exact runtime roles: grants, forced RLS, no table privilege, the HMAC, refusals for another facility/membership/old/rejected validation, malformed lists, sensitive values, purge). 0119_ocr_learning_rules.sql plus its runtime-grants.sql block (needs 0118). WHAT IT DOES: four new tables (ocr.learning_rules, ocr.learning_rule_showings, ocr.learning_switches, ocr.quality_summary_runs; no runtime privilege, RLS forced), one new SELECT policy on ocr.validations (ocr_validations_quality_summary, for the OCR functions' owner only, while its own transaction holds a summary-run row, which only ocr.review_outcome_summary writes, just before its read and deleted just after; without it the summary read nothing where the owner is neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS, as in production) and six functions. A rule switches on by itself only after at least 5 identical corrections from at least 3 staff with no conflicting correction in the last 180 days and after any retirement (facility rule at one facility; platform rule combined, from at least 2 facilities); it is a suggestion only, never a change to a saved value; it retires itself when 3 of its last 10 showings were not taken; owner kill switch per rule set, on by default, set only by a platform super admin (platform audit row admin.ocr.learning-switch.set). ocr.reading_suggestions returns the active rule per key for staff holding ocr.job.read. ocr.review_outcome_summary is the platform-wide phase-1 review-outcome summary (platform.admin.access and platform.operations.read, aggregate only, groups under 20 suppressed in SQL, audited). Owner decision Q43 of 2026-11-11 and the coordinator's answers (kept_unchanged neither support nor conflict; 180 days; combined platform evidence; re-arm only from evidence after retirement). Sensitive classes (ARVs/HIV, TB, psychiatric, sickle cell) are excluded in ocr-api: a document or review touching them stores nothing, and a sensitive value is never suggested (list hid.ocr.sensitive/v2: generic and brand names, PrEP/PEP, words). Showings are what the website says it displayed (the validation's optional shownSuggestions), never the rules found at save time, each bound to the reviewed reading's own item key, and the database records a showing only for a rule whose own key (field, read digest) is that one. ocr.purge_learning_showings lets the OCR worker apply the 180-day retention to showings. ocr-api calls the learning commands after the validation committed, in their own READ COMMITTED transaction (advisory locks per key and per rule). BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: existing reads of ocr.validations are unchanged (the new policy admits nothing outside a summary run, and nothing to any other role); older images never call the new functions. LOCKS: the new tables, SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.facilities, and ACCESS EXCLUSIVE NOWAIT (5 s bound, else 55P03) on ocr.validations for the policy. TESTS: services/ehr-api/test/database/ocr-learning-rules.integration.sql (69 cases, the summary under an owner that is neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS (lent to one where CI migrates as a superuser), and every suite also run with a migration login that is neither; cases: switch-on and every non-switch-on case, platform rule, precedence, kill switches, retirement, re-arm, refusals, summary suppression, the summary run and audit).
